usage: Select one compact technically grounded fact per appearance. The note/caveat is mandatory when material. The source is a pointer for follow-up verification, not a claim of browsing. Follow-ups can use practical_takeaway and safe_lab only on user-controlled resources.

items.line: HTTPS can protect the connection to a malicious website. Encryption does not establish the operator's good intentions.
items.practical_takeaway: Learn what TLS authentication does and does not establish.
items.safe_lab: Inspect the certificate details for a site you trust in your own browser. Record the issuer and subject.

items.line: A stolen valid session token can preserve access even when someone knows neither the password nor the authentication code. Revocation controls whether it keeps working.
items.practical_takeaway: Know the difference between account credentials and an active session.
items.safe_lab: Review the active-session list and sign-out options in one of your own accounts. Do not expose session tokens.

items.line: Encrypted DNS hides queries from some intermediaries. It does not hide those queries from the DNS resolver you chose.
items.practical_takeaway: Separate confidentiality from who performs DNS resolution.
items.safe_lab: Inspect your own device's DNS resolver settings; compare them to your browser's secure-DNS setting.

items.line: Internet routes are influenced by networks announcing which addresses they can reach. Bad announcements have redirected traffic belonging to other networks.
items.practical_takeaway: Understand routing announcements and the effect of route errors.
items.safe_lab: Look up a public AS number's announced prefixes on a read-only BGP viewer such as RIPEstat.

items.line: A website's cookie can identify a logged-in session without asking for the password again. The cookie is not the password, but possession can still matter.
items.practical_takeaway: Treat authenticated session cookies as secrets, not harmless personalization.
items.safe_lab: Inspect cookie attributes on a locally controlled demo webpage using browser developer tools.

items.line: A browser may tell a website which page you came from through a request header. The referrer policy determines how much of that address is exposed.
items.practical_takeaway: Recognize which URLs and origins can leak through navigation.
items.safe_lab: Inspect Referrer-Policy and Referer behavior using browser developer tools on pages you control.

items.line: A log records what a system was configured to observe. An empty log cannot prove that an event never happened.
items.source: NIST SP 800-92, Guide to Computer Security Log Management
items.practical_takeaway: Correlate alerts with configured telemetry rather than assuming completeness.
items.safe_lab: Generate a harmless event on a local test service, then locate it in its application log.

items.line: Multi-factor authentication can protect a login and still leave an existing compromised session usable. The two protections operate at different moments.
items.practical_takeaway: Understand why MFA and session revocation are separate controls.
items.safe_lab: Review your own account's active device/session dashboard and available session revocation controls.

items.line: A backup reachable with the same compromised credentials as its source may be lost in the same incident. Isolation is a recovery control.
items.practical_takeaway: Create backups that a single stolen account cannot erase.
items.safe_lab: Practice restoring a copy of a harmless file from a separate versioned backup.

items.line: A message can be encrypted while its timing, endpoints or routing metadata remain observable to some systems carrying it.
items.practical_takeaway: Separate confidential message content from delivery metadata.
items.safe_lab: View the full headers of an email you sent to yourself; identify timestamps and routing fields.

items.line: Certificate validation establishes a chain of trust in a server identity. It does not audit the software that server chooses to run.
items.practical_takeaway: Distinguish a valid trust chain from trustworthy site content.
items.safe_lab: Inspect the certificate chain of a website in your browser and compare that with the site's ownership claims.

items.line: A DNS change does not reach every computer at once. Cached answers can outlive a correction until their validity window expires.
items.practical_takeaway: Understand DNS TTL and propagation delay.
items.safe_lab: Use your device's DNS lookup utility on a public hostname and inspect the returned TTL if exposed.
